entries.input: Let $n$ be a positive integer. Prove that there are positive integers $a$, $b$, $c$ with $2a^{n} + 3b^{n} = 4c^{n}$ if and only if $n = 1$.
entries.name: Putnam2024A1
entries.title: Putnam 2024 A1

entries.input: Let $n$ be a positive integer. Prove that there are positive integers $a$, $b$, $c$ with $2a^{n} + 3b^{n} = 4c^{n}$ if and only if $n \leq 2$.
entries.name: Putnam2024A1Twin
entries.title: Putnam 2024 A1, answer set widened to $n \leq 2$
entries.rationale: A soundness twin for `putnam-2024-a1`: it admits $n = 2$ as well. The quadratic case is the one the 2024 solution rules out first, by reducing $a^{2} + c^{2} \equiv 0 \pmod 3$ on a primitive solution, so a model that agrees here is agreeing with the exact case the problem turns on. It states nothing the paper asked, so it cites no occurrence.

entries.input: For a positive integer $n$ let $k(n)$ be the number of $1$s in the base-$2$ expansion of $2023n$. Prove that the least value $k$ attains is $3$.
entries.name: Putnam2023B2
entries.conclusion: IsLeast {m : ℕ | ∃ n : ℕ, 0 < n ∧ (Nat.digits 2 (2023 * n)).sum = m} 3
entries.title: Putnam 2023 B2
entries.witness_note: The entry has no binders: it states one closed claim about a single set, so there is nothing for A6 to existentially close and a `trivial` witness would record coverage that was never obtained.

entries.input: For a positive integer $n$ let $k(n)$ be the number of $1$s in the base-$2$ expansion of $2023n$. Prove that the least value $k$ attains is $2$.
entries.name: Putnam2023B2Twin
entries.conclusion: IsLeast {m : ℕ | ∃ n : ℕ, 0 < n ∧ (Nat.digits 2 (2023 * n)).sum = m} 2
entries.title: Putnam 2023 B2, minimum lowered to two
entries.rationale: A soundness twin for `putnam-2023-b2`: $2$ is not attained, because $2023n = 2^{a} + 2^{b}$ would force $-1$ to be a power of $2$ modulo the factor $7$ of $2023$. Lowering a minimum by one leaves the claim looking exactly as plausible as the true one, which is the point. It states nothing the paper asked, so it cites no occurrence.

entries.name: Putnam2020B6
entries.title: Putnam 2020 B6

entries.input: Let $n$ be a positive integer. Prove that $\sum_{k=1}^{n} (-1)^{\lfloor k(\sqrt{2}-1) \rfloor} > 0$.
entries.name: Putnam2020B6Twin
entries.title: Putnam 2020 B6, inequality made strict
entries.rationale: A soundness twin for `putnam-2020-b6`: the partial sums do reach $0$, first at $n = 4$, where the floors are $0, 0, 1, 1$ and the four signs are $+, +, -, -$. Tightening $\geq$ to $>$ is the smallest possible perturbation of an inequality and cannot be spotted without evaluating the sum. It states nothing the paper asked, so it cites no occurrence.

entries.input: Let $A$ be the set of integers $n$ with $1 \leq n \leq 2021$ and $\gcd(n, 2021) = 1$, and for a nonnegative integer $j$ put $S(j) = \sum_{n \in A} n^{j}$. Prove that $2021$ divides $S(j)$ exactly when $j$ is a multiple of neither $42$ nor $46$.
entries.name: Putnam2021A5
entries.conclusion: (2021 ∣ ∑ n ∈ (Finset.Icc 1 2021).filter (fun n => Nat.gcd n 2021 = 1), n ^ j) ↔ ¬ (42 ∣ j) ∧ ¬ (46 ∣ j)
entries.title: Putnam 2021 A5

entries.input: Determine which integers have the form $A^{3} + B^{3} + C^{3} - 3ABC$ with $A$, $B$, $C$ nonnegative integers. Prove that an integer $n$ has this form exactly when $n \geq 0$ and $n$ is congruent to neither $3$ nor $6$ modulo $9$.
entries.name: Putnam2019A1
entries.title: Putnam 2019 A1

entries.input: Determine which integers have the form $A^{3} + B^{3} + C^{3} - 3ABC$ with $A$, $B$, $C$ nonnegative integers. Prove that an integer $n$ has this form exactly when $n \geq 0$.
entries.name: Putnam2019A1Twin
entries.title: Putnam 2019 A1, congruence condition dropped
entries.rationale: A soundness twin for `putnam-2019-a1`: dropping the modulus condition claims every nonnegative integer is represented, and $3$ is not. Nonnegativity is the half of the answer that is easy to see, so a model reading only that far agrees; the residues $3$ and $6$ modulo $9$ are the half that has to be proved. It states nothing the paper asked, so it cites no occurrence.
